newsitem.title: GERMANY: German "pyramid" investment fraud trial starts. [CORRECTED 12:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German "pyramid" investment fraud trial starts. [CORRECTED 12:10 GMT]

text.p: The four founding members of a so-called "pyramid" investment club went on trial on Thursday, accused of swindling 850 million marks (Corrects from 850,000 marks) ($560 million) from investors in Germany's largest ever criminal fraud.

Frankfurt state court lawyers accused Damara Bertges, former president of the European Kings Club, and three other club officials of a total 675,000 illegal bank dealings and 33,000 cases of deception.

Proceedings had to be adjourned soon after the start as Bertges, who was recently extradited to Germany from Switzerland to face trial, did not appear in court on time and was not expected to arrive until late afternoon.

The now-bankrupt European Kings Club is alleged to have amassed by deception a total of 850 million marks from 94,000 participants between 1991 and 1995, in an investment system promising an annual yield of 72 percent.

Investors had to pay 1,400 marks to join the Club, an outlay which was intended to guarantee them large returns starting with 2,400 marks in the first year. The aim was for an ever-increasing number of new investors to join the club creating a pyramid-shaped membership structure.
But the pyramid collapsed in late 1995, pushing European Kings Club into bankruptcy. Around 50,000 petitions from creditors have so far been filed against the club.
